title: A fair distinction opens a free question
meaning: Examining a familiar rule’s foundations can give your shared view a more accurate measure and the freedom of another question.
text: A familiar rule can have a boundary beyond which an interesting question begins. The Hierophant in the physical position of Ajna suggests discussing learned ways of assessing experience. Justice in energy supports examining a conclusion’s foundations and its proportion to observation. The Fool in emotions responds with freedom for another inquiry. Understanding need not begin with a ready formula.

For example, you use a familiar rule that an exhibition’s impact depends on what you remembered. Comparison reveals one object remembered through its awkward position although it was not particularly significant. **A fair distinction frees a question from its first ready answer.** You become interested in what stays in memory and why. The earlier principle retains some usefulness within a clearer boundary. Different reasons for remembering can be explored while significance remains distinct from an episode’s vividness. Accurate comparison of observations available to both of you makes the shared view more open.

The risk is turning a fresh question’s freedom into the claim that earlier ways of assessing mean nothing at all. Every answer then starts from zero. Proportion can preserve the principle’s working part. An exception refined its application while accumulated observations remain material. Free inquiry can continue the conversation through what you already understand while allowing other cases to contribute.
